brief.core_problem: Access tokens expire silently after 15 minutes. Users get a raw 401 with no recovery path — they must re-login manually, losing any in-progress work.
brief.stakeholders: End users: all authenticated users (~12k DAU). Business: Sarah Chen (PO), driven by Q3 SOC2 audit. Backend team owns AuthService. Mobile team blocked waiting for refresh flow.
brief.current_state: AuthService at src/services/auth.ts handles login via loginWithCredentials(). Express middleware at src/middleware/auth.ts:23 validates JWT but rejects expired tokens without refresh attempt. No refresh endpoint exists.
brief.desired_outcome: Seamless token refresh — users never see a 401 during normal usage. Refresh tokens rotate on use (SOC2 requirement).
brief.security_and_data: Tokens contain user_id (PII). Current tokens stored in localStorage (XSS risk). Refresh tokens should use httpOnly cookies. SOC2 requires token rotation.
brief.scale_and_performance: API handles ~200 req/s. New refresh flow must not add >50ms p99 latency. Token validation is on the hot path.
constraints: Backward compat with existing mobile app sessions
open_questions: Should we migrate existing localStorage tokens to httpOnly cookies?

reflections.text: We've confirmed the core problem and stakeholders. The security picture is clearer — SOC2 requires token rotation, and the current localStorage approach has XSS risk. What I'm less clear on is the deployment strategy and whether we need a migration for existing sessions.
How should we deploy this — rolling release or behind a feature flag? The mobile app's existing sessions complicate a big-bang switch.
I'm assuming we'll need a migration path for existing localStorage tokens — users shouldn't all be forced to re-login on deploy day.
